_help: Bot Checkup settings data. Every fix and every 'where to put your rules' entry must cite a source key from sources, and every source must be the vendor's own help, docs or announcement page that we opened on checked_on. Set path to null when the vendor does not document the exact steps, and say so in unverified. No made-up paths, no scores, no grades. scripts/test_bot_checkup.py enforces this.

assistants.name: Grok Bot
assistants.summary: Grok Bot uses connected apps and a shared cloud computer. Auto Review checks each action, and your own Ask first rules always stop a matching action for your OK.

fixes.title: Add Ask first rules for the actions you care about
fixes.why: Ask first rules always stop a matching action and show you an approval card. If an Ask first rule and an Allow rule both match, Ask first wins.
fixes.path: Settings → General → Bot → Auto-review (keep it on) → Custom Rules → under “It should:” choose Ask first → Add Rule

fixes.title: Set each connected app's send, post and delete tools to Needs approval or Blocked
fixes.why: Since v1.2.3 (Nov 18, 2026) each tool on a connector page can be Always allow, Auto-review, Needs approval or Blocked. Keep read-only tools you trust as they are.
fixes.path: Connect apps (sidebar) → select the connected count → open the app → set each tool
fixes.note: The four per-tool choices come from the changelog; the sidebar steps come from the Settings docs. Needs Grok Bot 0.70.2 or later.

fixes.title: Remove a saved card if you want to approve every payment
fixes.why: A card saved in Vault fills in at checkout without a separate approval each time.
fixes.path: Settings → Vault → select the card → remove it

fixes.title: Stop Bots running commands on your own computer
fixes.why: Access to the computer in front of you is separate from the Bot's cloud computer. The default is Ask every time; the docs suggest Never allow unless a Bot needs your local files.
fixes.path: Settings → Computer → Your computer → Execution on this computer → Never allow

fixes.title: Sign out of sites your Bots no longer need
fixes.why: All your Bots share one cloud computer, so a site signed in for one Bot is available to the others. The docs say separate Bots are not a security boundary.
fixes.unverified: There's no single settings switch for this in the docs. Ask your Bot to sign out of the site, or revoke the app in that service.

rules_home.text: Add each “Always ask me before” line as its own Ask first rule (one action per rule, up to 1,000 characters). Send the rest to your Bot in chat as a standing instruction.

assistants.name: ChatGPT dots
assistants.summary: A dot works on its own cloud computer with the apps you connect. An automatic review checks actions against your instructions, permissions and custom rules; some steps, like changing a password, always stay with you.

fixes.title: Add custom rules for sending, paying and deleting
fixes.why: Each rule picks one behavior: Take action without asking, Take action when you say so, Ask before taking action, or Hand off to you. Asking for a draft does not authorize sending it.
fixes.path: Desktop and web: Settings → Personalization → Custom rules (under Permissions) → Add. Phone: sidebar → Customize → Custom rules

fixes.title: Review plugin permissions for each connected app
fixes.why: Plugin permissions control app actions separately from custom rules. Rules don't grant or remove app access.
fixes.path: Custom rules → Open Plugins → Plugin permissions

fixes.title: Make purchases a Hand off to you rule if you want to finish every checkout yourself
fixes.why: With Wallet, OpenAI says you approve each payment with biometrics. A Hand off to you rule makes the dot ask you to take the action instead.
fixes.path: Settings → Personalization → Custom rules → Add → describe “buying or paying for anything” → Hand off to you

fixes.title: Check what your dot does in the background
fixes.why: Pausing a dot doesn't stop every delegated task or cancel scheduled runs. Each has its own stop control.
fixes.path: Desktop app: your dot's profile → Activity (stop a task) and Scheduled (disable or delete a recurring task)

fixes.title: Only connect your own computer if a task needs it
fixes.why: OpenAI says your computer stays separate from the dot unless you choose to connect it.
fixes.unverified: We couldn't find documented steps for disconnecting a personal computer from a dot. Workspace admins have an “Allow local computer access” switch.

rules_home.text: Add each “Always ask me before” line as its own custom rule set to Ask before taking action, and each “Never” line as Hand off to you. Tell your dot the rest in chat as an ongoing instruction.

assistants.name: Claude Duet
assistants.summary: Claude Duet runs on your Claude account, with the same memory and connectors. Anthropic says it is designed to ask before it sends a message, pays, signs a document or deletes anything.

fixes.title: Set connector tools to Needs approval or Blocked in Claude
fixes.why: Duet uses the connectors in your Claude account. Each connector has Tool permissions: Always allow, Needs approval or Blocked, per group of tools or per tool.
fixes.path: Claude → Customize → Connectors → select the connector → Tool permissions
fixes.note: The Tool permissions steps are from Claude's general connectors docs. The Duet article doesn't say whether Duet follows each per-tool choice.

fixes.title: Disconnect apps Duet doesn't need
fixes.why: Disconnecting stops access from then on, but Duet keeps memory of what it saw in earlier conversations.
fixes.path: Claude → Customize → Connectors → select the connector → Disconnect

fixes.title: Turn off past-chat search if you don't want Duet reading old chats
fixes.why: Duet searches your Duet chats and your Claude chats outside projects, using Claude's Search and reference chats setting.
fixes.path: Settings → Your Claude → Search and reference chats (older layout: Settings → Memory)

fixes.title: Know how Duet pays before you connect Link or Shop Pay
fixes.why: Anthropic says Duet asks before each purchase and uses a one-time card for each one. Link and Shop Pay are connected inside Duet, not in the connectors directory.
fixes.unverified: Anthropic's article doesn't list the steps to disconnect Link or Shop Pay from Duet.

rules_home.text: Send the rules to Duet in your main thread. Duet uses your Claude memory, but Anthropic's Duet article doesn't describe a separate rules or instructions setting, so check that it repeats them back.

assistants.name: Meta Muse
assistants.summary: Muse uses Connectors and the web. You set default permissions for connectors and websites, and each approval card offers choices from Allow once to Always allow.

fixes.title: Set Connectors to Always ask
fixes.why: Ask for some actions asks before every write action and important reads. Always ask asks before any action.

fixes.title: Set Web access defaults to Always ask
fixes.why: Always ask makes Muse ask before it opens any website. Ask for some actions only asks when your information may be shared or the site is unfamiliar.
fixes.path: Settings → Permissions → Web access defaults → Always ask

fixes.title: Revoke websites you allowed once and forgot
fixes.why: Choosing “Allow for this site” on an approval card lets Muse act on that site later without asking again. This list shows those sites and lets you revoke them.
fixes.path: Settings → Permissions → Manage permissions → Allowed websites

fixes.title: Make connectors read-only where Meta offers it
fixes.why: Meta says many Connectors can be set up so Muse only retrieves data and can't take actions, like sending a calendar invite.

fixes.title: Decide whether Muse reads new email on its own
fixes.why: Connecting email may let Muse read new emails as they arrive. Meta says you can change this in Settings.
fixes.unverified: Meta's help page says “in Settings” but doesn't name the exact screen.

rules_home.text: Send the rules to your Muse in chat. Meta says you can change its preferences any time by telling it, and recommends stating clear boundaries, like “Only search my email, not my text messages.”

assistants.name: Gemini Tasks
assistants.summary: Tasks in Gemini can use Connected Apps, Google Pay and Wallet, and a local or remote browser. Google says it always asks before sending, deleting, buying, paying or submitting forms.

fixes.title: Disconnect apps your tasks don't need
fixes.why: Tasks can use Connected Apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Google Pay and Wallet, and third-party apps.
fixes.path: gemini.google.com → sidebar → Customize (or More → Customize) → Connectors → the app → More options → Disconnect

fixes.title: Pause schedules that touch anything sensitive
fixes.why: Google says if a schedule runs while you're offline, you may not be able to stop an unintended action.
fixes.path: Open the task thread → scheduled task chip → More options → Pause (or use the Scheduled page on the web)

fixes.title: Delete the remote browser's saved sign-ins
fixes.why: When Gemini uses its remote browser, cookies with your sign-in details are kept for later sessions until you delete them or they expire.
fixes.path: gemini.google.com → Settings → Browser → Delete remote browser data → Delete

fixes.title: Turn off Chrome auto browse on computers you share
fixes.why: With your local Chrome, Gemini can reach every site you're signed in to.
fixes.path: Chrome → More → Settings → AI Innovations → Gemini in Chrome

fixes.title: Check bulk changes to Google Tasks reminders yourself
fixes.why: Google says Gemini can make bulk changes to your private Google Tasks without asking first.
fixes.unverified: There's no setting for this in Google's page. Review the request before you send it, or manage the reminders in Google Tasks yourself.

rules_home.text: Paste the rules into the task when you create it. Google calls reusable instructions “skills,” but we haven't checked the steps for saving one, so they aren't listed here.
rules_home.path: gemini.google.com → Task (below the text box) → describe the task
